newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus MPs seek inquiry into cement sale.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus MPs seek inquiry into cement sale.

text.p: Cypriot MPs asked for a parliamentary inquiry on Friday into plans by cement company Vassiliko to sell a large block of shares to Italy's Italcementi.

Parliament routinely accepts such requests. The inquiry, sought by members of the opposition communist party Akel and by members of the centre-right Democratic Party, a junior partner in the coalition government, will probably be undertaken by the parliamentary finance committee early next year.

"Bearing in mind the strategic importance of this product but also the international connections of the foreign company I think it is the duty of parliament and the state to investigate this serious issue," said Akel MP Kikis Kazamias.
Last week Vassiliko said it struck a deal with Italcementi whereby the Italian company will raise its stake in the Cypriot company to 33 percent from its current holding of 20 percent.

But Cyprus Cement Company has challenged the deal, saying that Vassiliko's majority shareholder, Greek Orthodox Archbishop Chrysostomos, reneged on a "gentleman's agreement" to sell Cyprus Cement the bulk of the Vassiliko shares.
MPs want the controversial deal debated before it is approved by the central bank, which examines all foreign investment applications in Cyprus.
"We are examining the matter," central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou told reporters. "We have not taken a decision yet."
